question: A shopkeeper mixes two kinds of sugar: one costing ₹30/kg and the other ₹50/kg. He mixes them in the ratio 3 : 2 by weight. At what price per kg should he sell the mixture so as to gain 25% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Weighted Average Cost Price (CP) = [(30 × 3) + (50 × 2)] ÷ (3 + 2)

CP = (90 + 100) ÷ 5 = 190 ÷ 5 = ₹38/kg

Required SP for 25% profit = 38 × 1.25 = ₹47.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹47.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price of Sugar₁ = ₹30/kg

Price of Sugar₂ = ₹50/kg

Mixing Ratio = 3 : 2

Desired Profit = 25%

**Formula:**

Mean Price (CP) = (Price₁ × Weight₁ + Price₂ × Weight₂) ÷ (Weight₁ + Weight₂)

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/90a93b0eb5a91dced514ed8b83aab493ac48c992e8d150ee7aba7c6fa6c8f9fb.png] 

⇒ Total Weight = 3 + 2 = 5 kg

⇒ Total Cost Price = (30 × 3) + (50 × 2) = 90 + 100 = ₹190

⇒ Mean CP per kg = 190 ÷ 5 = ₹38

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 38 × (125 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 38 × 1.25 = ₹47.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹47.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It states that (Quantity of Cheaper) ÷ (Quantity of Dearer) = (Price of Dearer − Mean Price) ÷ (Mean Price − Price of Cheaper).

Weighted Average Formula

The mean value Xₐvg of a mixture is given by (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂ + ... + nₙxₙ) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + ... + nₙ).

Profit Percentage

SP = CP × [ (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100 ]. Conversely, CP = [ SP × 100 ] ÷ (100 + Gain%).
